newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
SIX INDIANS AMONG 52 SURVIVORS OF AIR CRASH

Six of the 19 Indians who boarded the Ethiopian Airlines flight that crashed after being hijacked on Saturday have survived. Other survivors included the U.S. consul-general in Bombay, Franklin Huddle, and his wife. Giving details of the hijacking and subsequent crash, Ethiopian Airlines said on Saturday the Boeing 767 took off with 153 passengers on board from Addis Ababa for Abjdan via Nairobi. Nineteen minutes after take-off, the aircraft was hijacked.
The Hindustan Times
GOVERNMENT FORMATION IN UTTAR PRADESH AN UPHILL TASK

The newly-developed understanding between the non-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) parties may not make government formation in Uttar Pradesh any easier. The deal struck by the non-BJP parties for the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) polls was possible because none of the parties was capable of winning seats on its own. The plan was to keep the BJP at bay. The alliance is unlikely to last beyond the Upper House polls to see these parties combine to form a government in UP where the BJP is the single largest party.
Indian Express
POWER STRUGGLE IN CONGRESS PARTY HOTS UP

The tussle in the Congress party is hotting up. Partymen loyal to former Premier Narasimha Rao have decided to hit back at party chief Sitaram Kesri for his steps to divide the party. This follows Kesri's moves to sack Rao's loyalists from various party posts. The Rao camp is said to have held a meeting in Delhi to chalk out its strategy, the details of which were not immediately known. Kesri supporters Tariq Anwar and Madhav Rao Scindia hinted at further organisational changes in the party. Meanwhile, Congress leaders from Tamil Nadu met Sonia Gandhi, the widow of late former premier Rajiv Gandhi, and asked her to take over the party's leadership. Tamil Maanila Congress leader G K Moopa
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT ALLOWS MURDOCH TO SET UP SUBSIDIARY

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) cleared the proposal of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp to set up a wholly owned subsidiary. FIPB, however, put down a condition that News Corp would not be allowed to get into the broadcasting business in the country. News Corp would also not be allowed uplinking from India. Under the proposal, Murdoch would set up a cable TV company besides a programming base in the country.
TARIFF RATES TO BE AT GLOBAL STANDARDS BY 2003

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said Indian tariff rates would be brought down to the Asian levels by 2000, and to global standards by 2003. The announcement was made in response to complaints by Japanese businessmen on problems they faced in India. The minister also said any sharp cut in tariff rates would have adverse implication on India's fiscal deficit.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS OFFER AGENDA FOR CORPORATE GOVERNANCE

State owned financial institutions (FIs) have finalised corporate governance guidelines for nominee directors on corporate boards. The nominee directors appointed by the FIs are expected to play their roles in 19 major areas without interfering in day-to-day affairs of companies. The ares include investments in subsidiaries and loans, awards of contracts, mergers and acquisitions, dividend, expansion and diversification, subsidiarisation and desubsidiarisation and accounting policy. These guidelines aim at making owners and managers of companies more responsive to minority shareholders, promoters, institutional shareholders, deposit holders, creditors, consumers and the FIs.
REGULATORY BODY FOR NON-BANKING FINANCIAL FIRMS PLANNED

The central bank (RBI) has decided to create a separate instrument for regulating and supervising residuary and other non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The RBI has set up a working group which will hold meetings with the various residuary and other NBFCs, including chit funds, prior to framing a separate method to protecting deposit bases of members of the public in these companies. The group will review the role of residuary non-banking and other financial companies in tapping the deposits from members of public. It will also review their operational impact on the monetary and credit policies laid down by the RBI.
Financial Express
CHIDAMBARAN INDICATES STUDY OF PETROL PRICE HIKE

Foreign Minister P. Chidambaram indicated the government was considering, among other options, a hike in petrol prices in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) to meet the oil pool deficit. The government was considering various options in view of the rise in demand for petroleum products in the country, Chidambaram said in a television interview to be telecast on Wednesday.
INFLATION DOWN AT 6.47 PCT

Maintaining its downward trend for the second successive week, the annual rate of inflation fell by to 6.47 percent for the week ending November 9. Despite an increase in the major fuel, power, light and lubricants group index, the rate of inflation showed a fall during the week. The official Wholesale Price Index for all commodities (base 1981/82=100) for the week stood at 319.1 (provisional) as against 318.6 (provisional) for the previous week, recording a rise of 0.2 percent.
ITC SEEN ANNOUNCING BETTER RESULTS

Indian tobacco company ITC is likely to announce better results for April-September 1996. The improved results will be due to more than 20 percent growth in tobacco sales volume. According to market expectations, ITC's net profit may cross 1.7 billion rupees after 1.41 billion rupees in the previous corresponding period. Company sources said ITC's core operations had not been affected by the various conflicts at board level.
12 BLN RUPEE INCREASE IN FOOD SUBSIDY LIKELY

The Union food ministry has proposed an increase of 12 billion rupees in the food subsidy. This is likely to push up the subsidy burden in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) to 70.84 billion rupees an the original 58.84 billion rupees provided in the Budget. The ministry had requested a seven billion rupee hike in the subsidy to the finance ministry in November last. It proposes to seek another five billion rupees in February next year. The Observer
UNEMPLOYMENT MAY SOAR TO 35 MLN BY 1997

Contrary to claims that economic reforms mean more jobs, the unemployment rate has been rising. According to estimates, the backlog of unemployment in India would peak at 35 million by the end of the Eighth Plan (1992-97) from 23 million at the start of the plan. According to a study, the rate of employment generation continues to lag behind the growth of the labour force. Employment grew at an annual rate of 1.9 percent between 1990/91 (April-March) and 1995/96 against an annual rate of growth of 2.38 percent in the labour force. By the end of the Eighth Plan, there will be a 12 million backlog of unemployment to be cleared.
Business Standard
INDIAN CORPORATES FALL LOSE FAVOUR WITH FOREIGN INVESTORS

Foreign investors are losing interest in Indian conglomerates, sending their prices down on the international markets. Century Textiles last week became the latest victim of this trend after it dropped $17 in two days to $53. Two other Birla group companies, Grasim and Indian Rayon, also dropped sharply. Others, such as Raymond Woollen Mills and EID Parry, took a beating soon after they were issued. Larsen & Toubro, whose global depository receipt was at $20 in July, dipped to a low of $12 in early October.
20 PCT LIMIT SET ON FOREIGN EQUITY IN DEPOSITORIES

The finance ministry has decided on a 20 percent ceiling on foreign equity in the depositories, in line with the cap on foreign stake in banks. The government will have to incorporate the change since the depositories regulation issued by the bourse regulator does not stipulate a limit on foreign equity participation. The step to limit foreign stake in the depositories follows the finance minister's commitment made in parliament to the opposition.
AUTO FIRMS EXPECT EXPORTS TO TOUCH 19 BLN RUPEES

Twelve automobile companies, including Daewoo, Maruti Udyog, Telco and Hero Honda, have submitted export projections totalling over 19 billion rupees for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). This was stated by the commerce ministry. The ministry is studying the availability of area for parking of vehicles at ports, providing roll on and off carriers and self clearance/certification scheme for large car exporters to help meet the target. This problem is acute at the Bombay port through which 30,000 vehicles will be exported each year. The target for car exporters, as set by the ministry this year, is 18.72 billion rupees.
